goal: Build modelcluster to satisfy the complete public django-modelcluster specification.

atoms.title: Band cluster is queryable in memory and written only on save
atoms.input: Checker app defines Band(ClusterableModel) with a name CharField and BandMember(models.Model) with band = ParentalKey('Band', related_name='members', on_delete=CASCADE) and name. Build beatles = Band(name='The Beatles'); assign beatles.members = [BandMember(name='John Lennon'), BandMember(name='Paul McCartney')]; call beatles.members.count(); query Band.objects.filter(name='The Beatles') and BandMember.objects.count(); call beatles.save(); query both tables again.
atoms.expected: Before save: members.count() == 2, the Band filter is empty and no BandMember row exists. After save: one Band row and two BandMember rows whose band_id equals beatles.pk.

atoms.title: Offline editable install via setup.sh
atoms.input: In the pinned image with network disabled and PIP_NO_INDEX=1, copy the candidate tree, run its setup.sh, then from an unrelated empty directory import modelcluster and print modelcluster.__file__.
atoms.expected: setup.sh exits 0 without downloading or installing any dependency; the import resolves to the candidate's source tree (editable install).
gaps: Whether the candidate must author setup.sh or the benchmark harness supplies it is not stated: the text says the project 'is installed by a setup.sh' and that the candidate only needs to lay out the package so the editable install succeeds.
The packaging metadata format (pyproject.toml, setup.cfg or setup.py) is not specified.

atoms.title: Python 3.10 and Django 5.2 API compatibility
atoms.input: Under Python 3.10 with Django 5.2 and USE_TZ=True, import every public module, then call to_json() on a cluster whose model has an aware DateTimeField.
atoms.expected: All imports and the serialization succeed; no code path uses removed Django aliases such as django.utils.timezone.utc (no AttributeError or ImportError).
gaps: Only one removed API is named as an example; the set of disallowed pre-5.x APIs is not enumerated, so a check can only probe the code paths it exercises.

atoms.title: django-taggit used directly and declared as an extra
atoms.input: After the offline install, read the installed distribution metadata (Requires-Dist and Provides-Extra) and import modelcluster.contrib.taggit with the preinstalled django-taggit 6.1.
atoms.expected: django-taggit appears as a requirement conditioned on an extra; setup does not try to install it; modelcluster.contrib.taggit imports and uses taggit without error.
gaps: The name of the extra is not specified.
Whether django-taggit may additionally appear as an unconditional requirement is not stated explicitly; 'optional dependency' suggests it should not.

atoms.title: Exact public import paths
atoms.input: In a configured Django process run: from modelcluster.models import ClusterableModel, get_all_child_relations, get_all_child_m2m_relations; from modelcluster.fields import ParentalKey, ParentalManyToManyField; from modelcluster.queryset import FakeQuerySet; from modelcluster.utils import ManyToManyTraversalError; from modelcluster.forms import ClusterForm, childformset_factory, transientmodelformset_factory; from modelcluster.contrib.taggit import ClusterTaggableManager.
atoms.expected: Every import succeeds from exactly these module paths.
gaps: Whether 'modelcluster' must appear in INSTALLED_APPS (or ship an AppConfig) in the checker's settings is not stated.
Whether the modules must be importable before django.setup() is not stated.

atoms.title: Managers and fields are safe to subclass
atoms.input: Checker subclasses ParentalKey, ParentalManyToManyField and the manager class obtained via type(band.members), adding private attributes with generic names (e.g. _cache, _items, _parent, _field) to each subclass, then uses the subclassed field and manager to assign, query and save a cluster.
atoms.expected: Assignment, all(), add() and save() behave as for the unsubclassed classes; no public behaviour depends on a specific internal attribute name.
gaps: The private names the hidden tests may use are not stated, so collision safety can only be probed with chosen names.
The deferring manager class is not public; how tests obtain or install a subclassed manager is not specified.

atoms.title: ParentalKey is a ForeignKey defaulting to CASCADE
atoms.input: Declare BandMember.band = ParentalKey('Band', related_name='members') with on_delete omitted; inspect the field; save a Band with two members and delete the Band.
atoms.expected: The field is an instance of django.db.models.ForeignKey whose remote_field.on_delete is models.CASCADE; deleting the Band deletes its BandMember rows.

atoms.title: Assigning children replaces the in-memory set
atoms.input: band = Band(name='b') unsaved; band.members = [m1, m2]; then band.members = [m3]; read band.members.all(), m3.band and BandMember.objects.count().
atoms.expected: all() contains only m3 after the second assignment; each assigned child's band is the band instance; no BandMember row is written.

atoms.title: all() over touched, unsaved and saved parents
atoms.input: (a) Band() unsaved and untouched: band.members.all(); (b) after band.members = [m1]: type and contents of band.members.all(); (c) a Band saved with two members created through BandMember.objects.create, re-fetched with Band.objects.get(pk=...), untouched: band.members.all().
atoms.expected: (a) empty without error; (b) a modelcluster.queryset.FakeQuerySet containing m1; (c) the two database children (whether the result is a FakeQuerySet or a live QuerySet is unspecified).
gaps: For a saved, untouched parent the text says all() 'may' fall back to the live database queryset; the return type there is unspecified.

atoms.title: add() appends, replaces equal objects and de-duplicates
atoms.input: band.members = [m1, m2]; band.save(); m1_copy = BandMember.objects.get(pk=m1.pk); m1_copy.name = 'renamed'; band.members.add(m1_copy, m3_new); band.members.add(m2, m2).
atoms.expected: all() holds exactly three members: m1 (now with name 'renamed'), m2 and m3_new; no duplicates; the mutated instance replaced the equal one.
gaps: 'Equal object' is not defined; Django model equality (same concrete model and pk) is assumed, so equality of two distinct unsaved instances is unspecified.

atoms.title: remove(), clear(), create() and set() act in memory
atoms.input: Unsaved band with members [m1, m2, m3]: remove(m2); created = band.members.create(name='Ringo'); set([m4]); clear(). Count BandMember rows after each step.
atoms.expected: After remove: m1, m3. create returns a BandMember named 'Ringo' whose band is the parent, with pk None, now present in all(). After set: exactly m4. After clear: empty. No BandMember row is written at any step.

atoms.title: count() and the delegated FakeQuerySet read API
atoms.input: Unsaved band with three in-memory members named 'a', 'b', 'c': band.members.count(), .filter(name='b'), .exclude(name='b'), .get(name='c'), .order_by('-name'), .first(), .exists(), .values_list('name', flat=True).
atoms.expected: count() == 3 and every method returns the same result as calling it on band.members.all() over the in-memory set (filter yields b; order_by('-name') yields c, b, a).
gaps: 'The rest of the FakeQuerySet read API' is not enumerated for the manager; a check can only use a representative subset.

atoms.title: commit() syncs rows and requires a saved parent
atoms.input: Saved band with DB members m1, m2: set the in-memory members to [m1, m3_new] and call band.members.commit(). Separately: an unsaved Band with members [m4], call band.members.commit().
atoms.expected: After the first commit the DB holds m1 and m3_new with band_id == band.pk and m2's row is deleted. For the unsaved parent commit() raises django.db.IntegrityError and writes nothing.
gaps: Whether field edits made in memory to already-stored members are written by commit() is implied by 'write the in-memory set' but not stated explicitly.

atoms.title: In-memory children follow child Meta.ordering
atoms.input: Child model with Meta.ordering = ['name']; band.members = [child('Zed'), child('Amy')]; then band.members.add(child('Kim')).
atoms.expected: band.members.all() yields Amy, Zed after the assignment and Amy, Kim, Zed after add().

atoms.title: System check modelcluster.E001
atoms.input: Child model with a ParentalKey to PlainModel, a resolved models.Model that is not a ClusterableModel; run the field's check(). Control: a ParentalKey to a ClusterableModel.
atoms.expected: The result contains a django.core.checks.Error with id 'modelcluster.E001' and msg exactly 'ParentalKey must point to a subclass of ClusterableModel.'; the control yields no modelcluster.E001.

atoms.title: System check modelcluster.E002
atoms.input: Child model with ParentalKey(Band, related_name='+', on_delete=CASCADE); run the field's check().
atoms.expected: The result contains an Error with id 'modelcluster.E002' and msg exactly "related_name='+' is not allowed on ParentalKey fields".

atoms.title: Unresolvable target defers to fields.E300
atoms.input: Child model with ParentalKey('NoSuchModel', on_delete=CASCADE); run the model's check().
atoms.expected: Django's fields.E300 is reported and modelcluster.E001 is not.

atoms.title: ParentalManyToManyField holds the related set in memory
atoms.input: Article(ClusterableModel) with authors = ParentalManyToManyField(Author, related_name='articles_by_author'); saved authors a1, a2, a3. On an unsaved article: authors.add(a1, a2); remove(a1); set([a2, a3]); count(); inspect the through table; article.save(); then authors.clear(); inspect; article.save().
atoms.expected: The field is a ManyToManyField subclass. In memory: two after add, a2 after remove, a2 and a3 after set, count() == 2; no through rows before save; after the first save the through rows are exactly a2, a3; after clear() the DB still has them until the second save, after which none remain.

atoms.title: Assigning a parental m2m acts like set() on unsaved parents
atoms.input: Unsaved article: article.authors = [a1, a2]; then article.authors = Author.objects.filter(name__startswith='A'); inspect article.authors.all() and the through table; article.save().
atoms.expected: Each assignment replaces the in-memory set with exactly the given objects; nothing is written until save, after which through rows match the last assignment.

atoms.title: Manager model attribute and empty fresh read
atoms.input: article = Article(title='x') unsaved and untouched; read article.authors.model, list(article.authors.all()) and article.authors.count().
atoms.expected: article.authors.model is Author; the read returns an empty result and count() == 0 without raising.

atoms.title: add() rejects unsaved related objects
atoms.input: article.authors.add(Author(name='unsaved')) where that Author has no pk.
atoms.expected: ValueError is raised.

atoms.title: Parental m2m set follows target Meta.ordering
atoms.input: Author with Meta.ordering = ['name']; saved authors 'Zed' and 'Amy'; unsaved article.authors.set([zed, amy]).
atoms.expected: article.authors.all() yields Amy then Zed.

atoms.title: Reverse accessor reflects only saved parents
atoms.input: Saved author a1; unsaved article with authors = [a1]: read a1.articles_by_author.all(); save the article; read again and call a1.articles_by_author.filter(title='x').count().
atoms.expected: Before save the reverse accessor does not include the article; after save it does, and filter()/count() work as on a normal related manager.

atoms.title: value_from_object returns the in-memory set
atoms.input: Unsaved article with authors set to [a1, a2]; call Article._meta.get_field('authors').value_from_object(article).
atoms.expected: Returns the current in-memory related objects a1 and a2, not an empty result.
gaps: The container type returned (list, FakeQuerySet or another iterable) is unspecified.

atoms.title: save(update_fields) naming a parental m2m commits it
atoms.input: Saved article with authors [a1]; in memory set title='new' and authors = [a2]; call article.save(update_fields=['authors']).
atoms.expected: The through table holds only a2; the stored title is unchanged.

atoms.title: Direct FakeQuerySet construction
atoms.input: Three unsaved instances l1, l2, l3 of a plain checker model Log; qs = FakeQuerySet(Log, [l1, l2, l3]); evaluate list(qs), len(qs) and qs.filter on one field.
atoms.expected: list(qs) == [l1, l2, l3], len is 3, and read methods operate on the wrapped list although the instances are unsaved.

atoms.title: filter() and exclude() are complementary
atoms.input: FakeQuerySet over members named John, Paul, George, Ringo: f = qs.filter(name='John'); e = qs.exclude(name='John').
atoms.expected: f and e are new FakeQuerySet instances; f holds John and e the other three; together they equal qs and are disjoint; qs is unchanged.

atoms.title: Text and pattern lookups
atoms.input: FakeQuerySet over names 'John Lennon', 'Paul McCartney', 'george harrison': name='John Lennon' (implicit exact), name__exact, name__iexact='JOHN LENNON', name__contains='Mc', name__icontains='MC', name__startswith='Pa', name__istartswith='GEO', name__endswith='Lennon', name__iendswith='HARRISON', name__regex='^J.*n$', name__iregex='^G'.
atoms.expected: Each lookup returns what Django would: plain variants are case-sensitive and i-variants case-insensitive (contains 'Mc' and icontains 'MC' match Paul; regex '^J.*n$' matches John; iregex '^G' matches george).
gaps: Django regex semantics depend on the database backend; the text says 'Django-equivalent' without naming one, so only patterns with backend-independent meaning are checked.

atoms.title: Comparison, range, in and isnull lookups
atoms.input: FakeQuerySet over rows with integer score 1..5 and a nullable date: score__lt=3, score__lte=3, score__gt=3, score__gte=3, score__range=(2, 4), score__in=[1, 5], date__isnull=True, date__isnull=False, date__gte=date(2020, 1, 1).
atoms.expected: Django semantics: strict and non-strict bounds honoured, range inclusive at both ends (2, 3, 4), in matches the listed values, isnull partitions rows by None.

atoms.title: Value coercion, None/empty values and None inside in
atoms.input: Saved rows pk 1 name None, pk 2 name '', pk 3 name 'Flood': filter(id='2'); filter(name=None); filter(name=''); filter(name__isnull=True); filter(name__isnull=False); get(name__in=[None, 'Mink Car']); filter(name__in=[None, 'Flood']).
atoms.expected: id='2' matches pk 2; name=None only the None row; name='' only the empty-string row; isnull=True only the None row and isnull=False the other two; get(name__in=[None, 'Mink Car']) returns the None row; filter(name__in=[None, 'Flood']) returns the None and Flood rows.
gaps: Behaviour when coercion fails (e.g. id='abc') is unspecified.

atoms.title: Field named like a lookup token is a field
atoms.input: Checker model with an IntegerField literally named range; rows range=3 and range=7: filter(range=3); filter(range__gt=5).
atoms.expected: range=3 is an exact match on the field (the range=3 row); range__gt=5 applies gt to that field (the range=7 row); no error.

atoms.title: Relation traversal with None intermediates
atoms.input: Chef(name); Restaurant with a nullable proprietor FK (and a one-to-one variant) to Chef; Diner with a nullable favourite_restaurant FK. FakeQuerySet of diners including one with favourite_restaurant None and one whose restaurant has proprietor None: filter(favourite_restaurant__proprietor__name='Gordon'). Also on an unsaved band's in-memory members: filter(band__name='The Beatles').
atoms.expected: Only diners whose chain resolves to 'Gordon' are returned; rows with a None intermediate are excluded without raising; band__name matches the in-memory members through the relation to the parent.
gaps: Whether a None-intermediate row appears in exclude() is only implied by 'exclude returns the complement of filter'.

atoms.title: Matching relations against model instances
atoms.input: Saved band b1 and b1_again = Band.objects.get(pk=b1.pk): members.filter(band=b1_again). Two distinct unsaved bands u1, u2 with members pointing at u1: filter(band=u2). Multi-table inheritance Place -> Restaurant: rows with an FK to Place filtered by the Restaurant instance of the same pk, and rows with an FK to Restaurant filtered by the Place instance.
atoms.expected: filter(band=b1_again) returns b1's members (pk match); filter(band=u2) returns nothing; subclass and superclass instances sharing a pk match in both directions.

atoms.title: Q objects with AND, OR, XOR and negation
atoms.input: Rows named a, b, c with a boolean flag: filter(Q(name='a') | Q(name='b')); filter(Q(name='a') & Q(flag=True)); filter(Q(name='a') ^ Q(flag=True)); filter(~Q(name='a')); exclude(Q(name='a') | Q(name='b')); filter(Q(name='a') | Q(name='b'), flag=True).
atoms.expected: Results equal Django's: OR union, AND intersection, XOR rows matching exactly one operand, ~ complement, and positional Q combined with keyword lookups.
gaps: XOR over more than two operands is not described; Django's odd-parity meaning is assumed.

atoms.title: Many-to-many traversal raises ManyToManyTraversalError
atoms.input: FakeQuerySet(Article, [article]) where authors is a ParentalManyToManyField; evaluate list(qs.filter(authors__name='x')).
atoms.expected: modelcluster.utils.ManyToManyTraversalError is raised.
gaps: Whether the error is raised at filter() time or on evaluation is unspecified; whether a plain ManyToManyField or a direct comparison such as authors=a1 also raises is unspecified.

atoms.title: Date/time transforms in filter, get, values and values_list
atoms.input: Album rows with release_date DateField, Log rows with time DateTimeField, Alarm rows with t TimeField: filter(release_date__year=1999) and the iso_year, month, day, week, week_day, iso_week_day, quarter transforms; filter(time__date=date(2020, 1, 2)); filter(time__time=time(10, 30)); filter(t__hour=10), t__minute, t__second; get(release_date__month=3); values('release_date__year'); values_list('time__date', flat=True).
atoms.expected: Each transform equals the corresponding component of the Python value; values() and values_list() yield the derived values, keyed by the transform path in values() (e.g. {'release_date__year': 1999}).
gaps: Chaining a comparison after a transform (e.g. release_date__year__gte) is not stated.
For aware datetimes, the time zone in which date, time and hour are derived is not stated.

atoms.title: Weekday and ISO conventions and None datetimes
atoms.input: Rows with d = 2024-06-02 (Sunday), 2024-06-03 (Monday), 2021-01-01 and None: values('d__week_day', 'd__iso_week_day', 'd__week', 'd__iso_year', 'd__year').
atoms.expected: Sunday: week_day 1, iso_week_day 7. Monday: week_day 2, iso_week_day 1. 2021-01-01: iso_year 2020, week 53, year 2021. Every derived component of the None row is None.

atoms.title: get(), count(), exists(), first() and last()
atoms.input: FakeQuerySet over members a, b, c where b and c share a band: get(name='a'); get(name='zzz'); get(band=shared_band); values('name').get(name='a'); values_list('name').get(name='a'); count(); exists() on qs and on qs.filter(name='zzz'); first(); last().
atoms.expected: get returns the single match, raises the model's DoesNotExist for none and its MultipleObjectsReturned for two; after values()/values_list() get returns {'name': 'a'} / ('a',); count is 3; exists is True then False; first/last return the first and last row in the current order.
gaps: first() and last() on an empty queryset are not specified (Django returns None).

atoms.title: order_by(): multi-key, descending, relations, None first, random
atoms.input: Members with names and bands named 'B' and 'A', one member whose name is None: order_by('name'); order_by('-name'); order_by('band__name', '-name'); order_by('?').
atoms.expected: Ascending and descending by name; multi-key ordering applies keys in sequence across the band relation; the None-named row sorts first in ascending order; '?' returns a permutation of the same rows.
gaps: Placement of None values under descending ordering is not stated.

atoms.title: values() and values_list() shaping
atoms.input: Saved band b with members: qs.values(); qs.values('name', 'band', 'band__name'); qs.values_list('name', 'band'); qs.values_list('name', flat=True); qs.values_list('name', 'band', flat=True).
atoms.expected: values() yields one dict per row covering every concrete field; values('name', 'band', 'band__name') yields {'name': ..., 'band': b.pk, 'band__name': b.name}; values_list yields tuples in field order; flat=True yields scalars; flat=True with two fields raises TypeError.
gaps: The key used for a foreign key in no-argument values() (field name or attname) is not stated.
values_list() with no field names is unspecified.

atoms.title: distinct() by fields or by all non-pk fields
atoms.input: Saved rows (pk 1, name 'x', city 'A'), (pk 2, name 'x', city 'A'), (pk 3, name 'x', city 'B'): distinct(); distinct('name').
atoms.expected: distinct() keeps two rows (pk 1 and pk 2 collapse because they differ only by pk); distinct('name') keeps one row.
gaps: Which of the duplicate rows is kept is unspecified.

atoms.title: none(), all(), chaining and sequence protocol
atoms.input: qs with three rows: qs.none(); qs.none().filter(name='a').order_by('name').values('name'); qs.all(); qs.filter(score__gt=0).order_by('-name').values_list('name', flat=True); iterate qs; len(qs); qs[0]; bool(qs); bool(qs.none()).
atoms.expected: none() is empty and stays empty after chaining; all() returns the queryset itself with the same rows; chains compose; iteration yields the rows, len is 3, qs[0] is the first row, bool is True for non-empty and False for empty.
gaps: Whether all() must return the identical object (qs.all() is qs) or an equivalent queryset is ambiguous.

atoms.title: select_related/only/defer accepted; prefetch_related effective
atoms.input: On a FakeQuerySet call select_related('band'), only('name'), defer('name') and list() each. With three saved bands of two members each and saved articles with parental m2m authors, count queries (CaptureQueriesContext) while iterating Band.objects.prefetch_related('members') and Article.objects.prefetch_related('authors') and reading each parent's relation, versus the same loops without prefetch; also FakeQuerySet(Band, list_of_saved_bands).prefetch_related('members') then read each band's members.
atoms.expected: select_related, only and defer return querysets with the same rows; prefetched loops return the correct related objects with a query count that does not grow with the number of parents and is lower than the non-prefetched loop; FakeQuerySet.prefetch_related populates its results' relations so later reads issue no further queries.
gaps: Exact query counts are not stated, only that they are reduced.
Whether FakeQuerySet.prefetch_related returns a new queryset or acts in place is unspecified.

atoms.title: Abstract base with cluster keyword constructor
atoms.input: Inspect ClusterableModel._meta.abstract; build Band(name='The Beatles', members=[m1, m2], albums=[al1]) where members and albums are child relations, and Article(title='t', authors=[a1, a2]) with a parental m2m; count rows.
atoms.expected: ClusterableModel is abstract; name is set; band.members.all() holds m1, m2 with each child's band set to the instance; band.albums.all() holds al1; article.authors.all() holds a1, a2; nothing is written to the DB.

atoms.title: save() commits every child relation and parental m2m
atoms.input: Unsaved Band with members [m1, m2], albums [al1] and a parental m2m genres = [g1]; call band.save() once.
atoms.expected: The Band row, both member rows and the album row (FKs equal to band.pk) and the through row for g1 all exist.

atoms.title: save(update_fields) partitions relations and fields
atoms.input: Saved band; in memory change name, members and albums; call save(update_fields=['name', 'members']); inspect the DB; then save(update_fields=['albums']); inspect again.
atoms.expected: The first call writes name and commits members while albums stay unchanged in the DB; the second call commits albums. Relation names in update_fields raise no error.

atoms.title: get_all_child_relations includes inherited ParentalKey relations
atoms.input: Place(ClusterableModel) with child Review (ParentalKey related_name='reviews'); Restaurant(Place) multi-table child with MenuItem (ParentalKey related_name='menu_items'); Visit has a plain ForeignKey to Place. Call get_all_child_relations(Restaurant) and get_all_child_relations(Place).
atoms.expected: Restaurant's list contains the reviews and menu_items relations and Place's only reviews; Visit's plain FK relation is absent; each entry exposes name, get_accessor_name() ('reviews' / 'menu_items'), related_model (Review / MenuItem) and field (the ParentalKey).

atoms.title: get_all_child_m2m_relations lists ParentalManyToManyFields
atoms.input: Article(ClusterableModel) with authors = ParentalManyToManyField(Author) and links = models.ManyToManyField(Link); FeatureArticle(Article) adds categories = ParentalManyToManyField(Category). Call the helper on both models.
atoms.expected: Article: the authors field; FeatureArticle: authors and categories; the plain ManyToManyField is never listed; entries are field instances.

atoms.title: serializable_data structure with recursive children and m2m pks
atoms.input: Saved Band(name='B') with members [m1], albums [al1] where Album is itself a ClusterableModel with songs [s1], and parental m2m genres [g1, g2]; call band.serializable_data() and json.dumps(it, cls=DjangoJSONEncoder).
atoms.expected: A dict with 'pk' == band.pk, 'name' == 'B', 'members' == [m1's serialized dict], 'albums' == [a dict that itself contains 'songs': [s1's dict]], 'genres' == [g1.pk, g2.pk]; json.dumps succeeds.

atoms.title: Multi-table inheritance fields and shared pk in serialization
atoms.input: Place(ClusterableModel) with name; Restaurant(Place) with serves_hot_dogs; saved Restaurant(name='Joes', serves_hot_dogs=True); call serializable_data().
atoms.expected: The dict contains 'name' (declared on Place) and 'serves_hot_dogs'; 'pk' equals the id shared by the Restaurant and its Place row.

atoms.title: serialize=False omission and field-name keys for foreign keys
atoms.input: BandMember with ParentalKey band, a nullable FK favourite_restaurant and secret = CharField(serialize=False); Band with a parental m2m declared serialize=False and a child relation whose ParentalKey is declared serialize=False; serialize a member whose favourite_restaurant is None, and the band.
atoms.expected: The member dict has 'band' == band.pk and 'favourite_restaurant' == None, with no 'band_id', 'favourite_restaurant_id' or 'secret' keys; the band dict omits the serialize=False m2m and child relation.
gaps: How a child relation counts as 'declared serialize=False' (assumed: on its ParentalKey) is not stated.

atoms.title: to_json and from_json / from_serializable_data rebuild
atoms.input: Saved Band with members: s = band.to_json(); compare json.loads(s) with band.serializable_data(); rebuilt = Band.from_json(s) and Band.from_serializable_data(json.loads(s)); for a saved Restaurant(Place) r0, r = Restaurant.from_serializable_data(r0.serializable_data()).
atoms.expected: to_json() equals json.dumps(serializable_data(), cls=DjangoJSONEncoder) in content; rebuilt instances have the same pk and field values and their members relation holds instances with the serialized pks and values; r.pk, r.place_ptr_id and r.id (the root Place pk attribute) all equal r0's id.
gaps: from_json's remaining parameters are elided ('...'); forwarding of check_fks and strict_fks is implied, not spelled out.

atoms.title: check_fks resolution of dangling foreign keys
atoms.input: Serialize clusters, then delete referenced rows and deserialize with check_fks=True: (a) a child with an on_delete=SET_NULL FK; (b) two children with a non-parental CASCADE FK, one dangling; (c) a base object with a nullable SET_NULL FK; (d) a base object with a nullable CASCADE FK, once with strict_fks=False and once with strict_fks=True.
atoms.expected: (a) the child is kept with the FK None; (b) the dangling child is dropped and the other kept; (c) the base FK is None; (d) strict_fks=False gives a base FK of None, strict_fks=True makes from_serializable_data return None.
gaps: Behaviour with check_fks=False is not described.
on_delete values other than SET_NULL and CASCADE (e.g. PROTECT) are not described for child objects.
Nullifying a non-nullable dangling base FK is not addressed.

atoms.title: Deserialized children re-sorted by Meta.ordering
atoms.input: Child model with Meta.ordering = ['name']; hand-built serializable data listing members 'Zed' then 'Amy'; Band.from_serializable_data(data).
atoms.expected: band.members.all() yields Amy then Zed.

atoms.title: Datetimes serialized as UTC and restored to local time
atoms.input: Settings USE_TZ=True, TIME_ZONE='Asia/Seoul' (UTC+9); model with a DateTimeField; instances holding naive datetime(2024, 1, 1, 9, 0), aware 2024-01-01 12:00+02:00, and None; to_json() then from_json().
atoms.expected: The JSON holds ISO strings ending in 'Z' for 2024-01-01 00:00 UTC and 2024-01-01 10:00 UTC, and null; from_json yields datetimes for the same instants expressed in Asia/Seoul time, and None.
gaps: Whether serializable_data() already holds the UTC ISO string or only to_json() does is not stated.
Behaviour with USE_TZ=False and exact ISO formatting (e.g. microseconds) are not specified.

atoms.title: FileField survives a JSON round-trip
atoms.input: Model with a FileField and MEDIA_ROOT in a temporary directory; instance whose file was saved as 'docs/a.txt' with content b'hello'; to_json() then from_json().
atoms.expected: The rebuilt instance's file has the same name and opening it yields b'hello'.
gaps: 'FileField contents' may mean the stored file name/reference or the file bytes; the text does not say whether bytes are embedded in the JSON.

atoms.title: copy_cluster returns an unsaved deep copy and a map
atoms.input: Saved Band(name='B') with members [m1, m2], albums [al1 with songs [s1]] (Album clusterable), parental m2m genres [g1] and a plain ManyToManyField fans [f1]; copy, child_map = band.copy_cluster(); then copy.save().
atoms.expected: Before save copy.pk is None; name equals 'B'; copy.members holds two new instances with pk None, band == copy and the original names; the copied album has pk None and its songs are copied with pk None; copy.genres holds g1; the original band is unchanged; child_map maps (members relation, m1.pk) and (members relation, m2.pk) to the new members. After copy.save(), copy.fans is empty.
gaps: The meaning of the exclude_fields parameter is not described.

atoms.title: copy_child_relation overwrite, append and commit
atoms.input: Source band with members [m1, m2]; target band with members [t1]: source.copy_child_relation('members', target); on a fresh target, source.copy_child_relation(rel_obj, target, append=True) where rel_obj comes from get_all_child_relations(Band); with commit=True on a saved target; with commit=True on an unsaved target.
atoms.expected: Default: target.members holds only copies of m1 and m2 (pk None, band == target). append=True: t1 plus the copies. commit=True on a saved target writes the copies' rows immediately; on an unsaved target it raises IntegrityError.
gaps: The error for a relation that is not a ParentalKey relation is not specified.

atoms.title: copy_child_relation returned object map
atoms.input: Saved source band whose stored member m_saved has a pk, plus an in-memory unsaved member m_new; result = source.copy_child_relation('members', target).
atoms.expected: result[(rel, m_saved.pk)] is the copy of m_saved; result[(rel, None)] is a list containing the copy of m_new.
gaps: Whether rel in the key is the relation object or the accessor string passed by the caller is not stated.

atoms.title: copy_all_child_relations with exclude
atoms.input: Source band with members [m1] and albums [al1]; target band: result = source.copy_all_child_relations(target, exclude=['albums']); repeat on a fresh target without exclude.
atoms.expected: With exclude: target.members holds a copy of m1, target.albums is untouched and result has entries for members only. Without exclude: both relations are copied and result merges the entries of both.

atoms.title: transientmodelformset_factory tolerates absent pks
atoms.input: FormSet = transientmodelformset_factory(BandMember, fields=['name']); bound data form-TOTAL_FORMS=2, form-INITIAL_FORMS=0, form-0-name='A', form-1-name='B' with no id values; is_valid(); objs = formset.save(commit=False).
atoms.expected: The formset is valid and save(commit=False) returns two unsaved BandMember instances named A and B; no row is written.
gaps: How initial in-memory instances are supplied (queryset=, initial=) and the default formset= base class are not stated.

atoms.title: childformset_factory binds to a parent via ParentalKey
atoms.input: FS = childformset_factory(Band, BandMember, fields=['name']), and the factory called with each documented keyword (fk_name, exclude, extra, can_order, can_delete, max_num, validate_max, min_num, validate_min, widgets, inherit_kwargs, formsets, exclude_formsets, formfield_callback); fs = FS(instance=band) for a saved band with two members.
atoms.expected: The factory accepts the documented signature; 'band' is not a form field; fs has two forms initialised from the existing children followed by three blank extra forms.
gaps: Whether in-memory unsaved children of an unsaved parent count as 'existing children' is not stated.

atoms.title: Child formset save stages to memory or commits
atoms.input: Saved band with members m1, m2; bound child formset data editing m1's name, marking m2 DELETE and adding a member; fs.save(commit=False); inspect the DB and band.members.all(); band.save(). Repeat with fresh data and fs.save(commit=True).
atoms.expected: commit=False: the DB is unchanged while band.members.all() shows the edit and the addition and no longer contains m2; after band.save() the DB matches. commit=True: the DB reflects all three changes immediately.

atoms.title: max_num/min_num enforced only with validate flags
atoms.input: Child formset with max_num=2 bound with three filled forms, without and with validate_max=True; min_num=2 bound with one filled form, without and with validate_min=True.
atoms.expected: Without the flags both formsets are valid; with validate_max the formset is invalid with a non-form error coded 'too_many_forms'; with validate_min it is invalid with code 'too_few_forms'.

atoms.title: sort_order_field enables ORDER and writes it
atoms.input: Child model with sort_order_field = 'sort_order' and a nullable IntegerField sort_order; childformset_factory without can_order; bound data with ORDER 2 and 1 for two new forms; save(commit=False).
atoms.expected: The forms include an ORDER field; the saved children carry sort_order 2 and 1 matching their submitted ORDER values.
gaps: How sort_order_field is declared on the child model (class attribute name and value) is only implied by its name.

atoms.title: Nested child formsets via form=ClusterForm
atoms.input: Album(ClusterableModel) child of Band with a Song child of Album; FS = childformset_factory(Band, Album, form=ClusterForm, formsets=['songs'], fields=['title']); bound data with one album and two songs; save(commit=False); band.save().
atoms.expected: Each album form exposes a songs formset; after band.save() the album and its two songs exist with correct FKs.
gaps: The bound-data prefix scheme for nested formsets is not stated.

atoms.title: Default 'form' prefix for standalone child formsets
atoms.input: FS = childformset_factory(Band, BandMember, fields=['name']) bound without prefix= using keys form-TOTAL_FORMS, form-INITIAL_FORMS, form-0-name; a ClusterForm for Band with Meta.formsets = ['members'] bound with members-TOTAL_FORMS, members-INITIAL_FORMS, members-0-name.
atoms.expected: The standalone formset reads the 'form-' keys (its prefix is 'form') and is valid; the ClusterForm-managed formset uses the prefix 'members'.

atoms.title: Meta.formsets as a list or a dict of options; none by default
atoms.input: Band ClusterForms: A with Meta.formsets = ['members']; B with Meta.formsets = {'members': {'fields': ['name'], 'widgets': {'name': Textarea}}, 'albums': {'form': AlbumClusterForm, 'formsets': ['songs']}}; C with Meta.formsets = {'members': {'formset_name': 'records'}}; D with only Meta.fields.
atoms.expected: A builds a members formset only; B's member forms render only name, with Textarea, and its album forms are AlbumClusterForm instances with a nested songs formset; C is accepted (observable effect of formset_name unspecified); D builds no child formsets.
gaps: The effect of the formset_name option is not described.
Dict option 'exclude_formsets' for nesting is listed without separate semantics; assumed to mirror Meta.exclude_formsets.

atoms.title: Meta.exclude_formsets
atoms.input: Band ClusterForm with Meta.exclude_formsets = ['albums'] where Band has child relations members and albums.
atoms.expected: A formset is built for members only.

atoms.title: Meta.widgets child-relation key
atoms.input: Band ClusterForm with Meta.formsets = ['members'] and Meta.widgets = {'name': TextInput(attrs={'class': 'parent'}), 'members': {'name': Textarea}}.
atoms.expected: The parent's name uses the TextInput with class 'parent'; each member form's name uses Textarea.

atoms.title: Inherited child relations get formsets
atoms.input: Place(ClusterableModel) with child relation reviews; Restaurant(Place) with child relation menu_items; Restaurant ClusterForm with Meta.exclude_formsets = ['menu_items'], and another with Meta.formsets = ['reviews', 'menu_items'].
atoms.expected: The first form has a reviews formset (inherited relation included); the second has both.

atoms.title: formsets attribute on class and instance; three extra forms
atoms.input: BandForm with Meta.formsets = ['members', 'albums']; NoFormsetForm with none configured; inspect BandForm.formsets, NoFormsetForm.formsets, form = BandForm(instance=Band()) and form.formsets['members'].
atoms.expected: BandForm.formsets is a dict with keys members and albums mapping to formset classes; NoFormsetForm.formsets == {} and is falsy; form.formsets has the same keys holding formset instances; the unbound members formset for a new Band has three extra forms.

atoms.title: Composite validation, child uniqueness and deleted forms
atoms.input: Bound BandForm with a members formset: (a) valid parent, one member form missing its required name; (b) invalid parent, valid members; (c) two member forms with the same name where BandMember has unique_together ('band', 'name'); (d) the same with a Meta.constraints UniqueConstraint on ('band', 'name'); (e) an invalid member form marked DELETE next to valid data; (f) all valid with distinct names.
atoms.expected: (a) to (d) is_valid() is False, (c) and (d) reporting the duplicate; (e) and (f) is_valid() is True, the deleted form not being validated.
gaps: The error message and placement for child uniqueness violations are not stated.

atoms.title: as_p, media and is_multipart aggregate children
atoms.input: BandForm with a members formset whose form uses a widget with Media(js=['child.js']) and a parent widget with Media(js=['parent.js']); a variant whose child model has a FileField.
atoms.expected: as_p() returns a SafeString containing the parent's fields before the member forms; form.media includes parent.js and child.js; is_multipart() is False for the first form and True for the FileField variant.
gaps: The exact HTML of as_p() (management form placement, formset markup) is not specified.

atoms.title: Constructor kwargs reach child forms only via inherit_kwargs
atoms.input: BandForm(instance=band, label_suffix='!!') with Meta.formsets = {'members': {'fields': ['name']}} versus {'members': {'fields': ['name'], 'inherit_kwargs': ['label_suffix']}}; read each member form's label_suffix.
atoms.expected: Without inherit_kwargs member forms keep the default label_suffix; with it each member form has label_suffix '!!'.
gaps: How a custom (non-ModelForm) constructor kwarg reaches ClusterForm, and whether ClusterForm accepts unknown kwargs itself, is not stated.

atoms.title: ClusterForm.save with commit=True/False and save_m2m
atoms.input: ArticleForm for Article(ClusterableModel) with a child-relation formset, parental m2m authors, a ClusterTaggableManager tags field and a plain ManyToManyField links; valid bound data. (1) obj = form.save(commit=False); inspect DB and obj; obj.save(); form.save_m2m(). (2) A fresh bound form: form.save().
atoms.expected: (1) After save(commit=False) nothing is written while obj's children, authors and tags reflect the data in memory; obj.save() writes the instance, children, authors and tags; links are written only by save_m2m(). (2) save() writes the instance, children, authors, tags and links.

atoms.title: clusterform_factory helper
atoms.input: FormClass = clusterform_factory(Band, fields=['name']) imported from modelcluster.forms; instantiate it with instance=band.
atoms.expected: Returns a ClusterForm subclass for Band exposing the name field, analogous to modelform_factory.
gaps: clusterform_factory is not listed in the public import surface; its module (assumed modelcluster.forms) and accepted kwargs (e.g. formsets) are not stated.

atoms.title: ClusterTaggableManager declared with a ParentalKey through model
atoms.input: TaggedPlace(taggit TaggedItemBase) with content_object = ParentalKey('Place', related_name='tagged_items', on_delete=CASCADE); Place(ClusterableModel) with tags = ClusterTaggableManager(through=TaggedPlace, blank=True); run model checks; place = Place(name='p'); place.tags.add('a'); count TaggedPlace rows; place.save().
atoms.expected: ClusterTaggableManager is a subclass of taggit's TaggableManager; checks pass; the tag is held in memory with no TaggedPlace row until place.save(), after which a TaggedPlace row links place and tag 'a'.

atoms.title: Tag operations in memory on unsaved and saved instances
atoms.input: Unsaved place: tags.add('a', 'b'); remove('a'); set(['b', 'c']); count(); list(all()); clear(); set(['x']); record TaggedPlace rows throughout; place.save(). Then change tags on the saved place and check rows before a second save.
atoms.expected: all() and count() track the in-memory state (b; then b, c with count 2; then empty; then x) and all() yields taggit Tag instances; TaggedPlace rows change only on save(), after which they match the final tag set.
gaps: Whether looking up or creating Tag rows during add()/set() counts as touching the database is not stated; the check observes tagged-item rows only.

atoms.title: Non-string, non-Tag values rejected
atoms.input: place.tags.add(1) on an unsaved place; control: place.tags.add(Tag.objects.create(name='t')).
atoms.expected: add(1) raises ValueError; adding a Tag instance is accepted.

atoms.title: prefetch_related('tags') over owners
atoms.input: Three saved places with distinct tags; iterate Place.objects.prefetch_related('tags') reading list(place.tags.all()) under CaptureQueriesContext, then repeat with five places.
atoms.expected: Each place yields exactly its own tags and the query count is the same for three and five places.

atoms.title: Tag fields through ClusterForm, cluster-aware and plain
atoms.input: PlaceForm(ClusterForm) with fields ['name', 'tags'] bound with tags='a, b'; obj = form.save(commit=False); inspect memory and DB; obj.save(). Separately a ClusterableModel with a plain taggit TaggableManager and its ClusterForm bound with tags='x, y'; form.save().
atoms.expected: ClusterTaggableManager: obj.tags in memory are a and b before any write and TaggedPlace rows exist after obj.save(). Plain TaggableManager: after form.save() the instance has tags x and y in the DB.
gaps: When a plain TaggableManager's tags are applied under ClusterForm.save(commit=False) is not stated.

integration.scenario: Build a cluster in memory, query it, save it, mutate it and save again.
integration.input: Band(name='B', members=[m1, m2], genres=[g1]) via the constructor; query band.members.filter/order_by/get and band.genres.all(); band.save(); then band.members.remove(m1), band.members.create(name='m3'), band.genres.set([g2]); query again; band.save().
integration.expected: Queries before the first save reflect the in-memory cluster while the DB is empty; after the first save the band, two members and the g1 link exist; after the mutations queries show the new state while the DB still holds the old one; after the second save m1's row is deleted, m3 exists and the only link is g2.

integration.scenario: In-memory FakeQuerySet results match Django's database results for the same chains.
integration.input: Build an unsaved cluster whose children have text, numeric, date and FK fields; run a fixed battery of chains (text, range and comparison lookups, Q with OR/XOR/negation, relation traversal, date transforms, order_by, values_list) on band.members; save; run the identical chains on BandMember.objects.filter(band=band) in SQLite.
integration.expected: Each in-memory result equals the database queryset's result (rows or values, and order where an order_by is applied); the documented in-with-None divergence is excluded from the battery.

integration.scenario: Serialize a multi-table-inheritance cluster with nested children, m2m and datetimes, rebuild it and compare.
integration.input: Saved Restaurant(Place) with name, an aware DateTimeField, children (one clusterable with grandchildren and Meta.ordering), a parental m2m and a nullable FK; s = r.to_json(); r2 = Restaurant.from_json(s); compare r2.serializable_data() with r.serializable_data(); r2.save() and reload from the DB.
integration.expected: The rebuilt instance serializes identically to the original; children follow Meta.ordering; every pk attribute up the inheritance chain equals the original id; after r2.save() the DB holds the same cluster without duplicate rows.

integration.scenario: Copy a saved cluster and save the copy as an independent cluster.
integration.input: Saved band with members, nested albums/songs and a parental m2m; copy, child_map = band.copy_cluster(); copy.name = 'Copy'; copy.save(); then other = Band(name='O'); other.save(); band.copy_all_child_relations(other, commit=True).
integration.expected: After copy.save() the DB holds two independent clusters: the original rows unchanged and new member, album and song rows pointing at the copy, with the same m2m targets; each child_map value now has a pk different from its key's original pk; copy_all_child_relations(commit=True) writes rows for other immediately.

integration.scenario: Edit a two-level cluster through a ClusterForm with nested formsets and save in two phases.
integration.input: BandForm with Meta.formsets = {'albums': {'form': AlbumClusterForm, 'formsets': ['songs']}, 'members': {'fields': ['name']}} on a saved band; bound data editing one member, deleting another, adding an album with two songs; is_valid(); obj = form.save(commit=False); inspect the DB; obj.save().
integration.expected: is_valid() is True; after save(commit=False) the DB is unchanged while obj's relations show the edits; after obj.save() the member, album and song rows match the submitted data.

integration.scenario: A tagged cluster is saved and read back with prefetching.
integration.input: Unsaved Place with tags set(['a', 'b']) and child reviews; save; create further places likewise; iterate Place.objects.prefetch_related('tags', 'reviews') under query counting for two different numbers of places.
integration.expected: After save the tagged-item and review rows exist; the prefetch loop returns each place's own tags and reviews with a query count independent of the number of places.
